claims.text: The starting material is additively manufactured, cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock.
As-built additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi typically contains residual thermal stresses.
As-built additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi typically exhibits segregation and defect formation.
The proposed intervention is annealing at approximately 700 °C for about one hour in an inert atmosphere.
A short anneal near 700 °C will relieve residual stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
The anneal will homogenize the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure through limited atomic diffusion.
Annealing near 700 °C for one hour is sufficiently mild to avoid significant elemental segregation.
The anneal will lower dislocation density by enabling limited atomic rearrangement and dislocation reorganization.
Dislocation rearrangement redistributes local strain energy and permits lattice relaxation.
Constrained diffusion during the anneal will prevent defect growth.
The anneal will preserve overall phase stability and avoid phase destabilization.
Annealed samples will have lower residual stress than the untreated baseline.
Annealed samples will have lower defect density than the untreated baseline.
Annealing will improve ductility and overall mechanical integrity.
Partial dislocation rearrangement may cause a minor reduction in yield strength.
The proposed response is valid only for samples made under rapid-solidification conditions and additive-manufacturing parameters similar to those tested.
Higher-temperature or longer-duration annealing may produce substantial segregation or phase destabilization.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and predicted outcome describe comparison with conventionally processed or conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, but the stated baseline and experiment compare annealed additively manufactured samples with unannealed additively manufactured samples. Thus the experiment cannot establish superiority over a distinct conventional-fabrication route.
